title: Gravel Bike Suspension, is it a step too far? - FIrst Look at the LightCarbon LCG087

takeaways.text: He chose the optional crackle paint for roughly US$100–130 extra over the standard matte or gloss black.
The elastomer micro-suspension is compliance, not suspension: it takes the buzz out of rough ground with no pedal bob or sag he could provoke when climbing.
His rear caliper needed spacers to sit far enough over; LightCarbon now lists L-TWOO calipers as incompatible and recommends Shimano, SRAM or TRP.
Repeats the maker's figures: size-M frame 1,480 g ±40 g, seatpost 316 g, T47 85.5 mm, 700×47C or 650B×1.95 in tires; his 47 mm tires show plenty of room.
UDH hanger; a spare suspension elastomer cost him US$10, which he recommends ordering with the frame.

disclosure: Owner video; no supply arrangement or sponsorship is stated.
summary: First look and first gravel ride on a size-M LightCarbon LCG087-D with rear micro-suspension, built with SENSAH SRX Pro 1×12.
